_comment: Select models by task difficulty; the spawning home chooses the effort, and omp connects directly to each provider. Codex models draw on a separate quota pool from Anthropic, so use them when the Anthropic weekly quota is tight (omp usage).

rules.when: Mechanical or small, well-specified work: typo and copy fixes, renames, docs-only edits, config or version bumps, moving files, formatting, data collection, simple scripted checks, or a narrow one-file change with an obvious fix.

Ordinary engineering: a normal feature, bug fix with a known or quickly findable cause, UI change, tests, refactors in one area, PR follow-ups and review fixes, release chores, or a routine investigation or scout report.
rules.why: The everyday tier; usually medium thinking, high when the change spans several files. Sonnet 5.5 comes first. gpt-6.1-sol only when the Anthropic quota is exhausted (omp usage).

rules.when: Genuinely hard work only: architecture or design across many components, security- or money-sensitive code, concurrency, data migrations, client production paths with a large blast radius, a bug whose cause is unknown after a first look, or a task a cheaper model already failed.
rules.why: Opus 5.5 is reserved for hard tasks; high or xhigh thinking.
